questions.explanation: Forests are valuable both economically and ecologically.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The movement of people out of their own country or region to settle elsewhere is called
questions.explanation: Emigration refers to moving out, and immigration to moving in.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Areas with difficult terrain, such as high mountains, generally have
options: A larger share of cities than the plains
questions.explanation: Rugged land and cold climate make farming and travel difficult, so fewer people live there.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which of the following is a push factor for migration from a village?
options: Lack of employment in the village
questions.explanation: Push factors make people want to leave their place, such as unemployment or poverty.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which people are counted as dependants in the age structure of a population?
questions.explanation: Dependants are children and old persons who depend on the working-age group.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why did India's population begin to grow rapidly after 1921?
options: Death rates fell due to better health facilities and food supply, while birth rates remained high
questions.explanation: A falling death rate with a high birth rate causes growth.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What is meant by literacy rate?
questions.answer: The literacy rate is the share of the population aged seven years and above that can read and write with understanding.
keyPoints: Share of population who can read and write
Counted for ages seven and above
questions.explanation: It is a key indicator of the quality of population.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why is the sex ratio considered an important indicator of the status of women in a society?
questions.answer: A low sex ratio suggests that girls are neglected, are given less care or are not given equal chances compared with boys. A higher ratio generally indicates better respect and care for women.
keyPoints: Low ratio suggests neglect or discrimination
questions.explanation: The sex ratio reflects social attitudes toward girls and women.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which of the following is a feature of a dictatorship?
options: Citizens can remove the ruler by vote
The ruler cannot be removed by the citizens
questions.explanation: A dictator holds power without being answerable to the people.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What is a government in which a monarch's powers are limited by a constitution and an elected parliament called?
questions.explanation: In a constitutional monarchy, elected representatives hold real power.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: How can democracy improve the quality of decisions?
options: By requiring consultation and discussion with many people
questions.explanation: Consultation brings in different views and reduces mistakes.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: A country holds elections, but the ruling party controls all the media and stops rivals from holding rallies. Why are these elections not free and fair?
options: Because voting takes place in the morning
Because the voters are too many
Because parties and candidates do not have equal freedom to compete
questions.explanation: Free and fair elections require an equal chance for all candidates and open information.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Democracies may take time to make decisions. Which statement is the best evaluation?
options: Consultation takes time but it can prevent hasty and harmful decisions
Decisions in a democracy are never made
Speed is the only thing that matters
questions.explanation: Discussion may be slower, but it can lead to decisions that are better accepted.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Give two arguments commonly made against democracy and one reply to them.
questions.answer: Critics say that democracy leads to frequent changes of leaders and political instability and that decisions are delayed by discussion. In reply, supporters say that regular change allows the removal of poor rulers, and that discussion leads to decisions that more people accept.
keyPoints: Reply: change allows removing poor rulers or wider acceptance
questions.explanation: Democracy has costs, but its supporters see them as worth bearing.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: How does democracy promote equality and dignity among citizens?
questions.answer: Democracy gives every adult one vote of equal value regardless of wealth or social background, and it guarantees rights. This allows ordinary people to raise their voice and be treated as equals.
questions.explanation: Political equality is the base of democratic dignity.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: About how long did the Constituent Assembly take to frame the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: It took about two years, eleven months and eighteen days.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: On which island prison was Nelson Mandela held for many years?
questions.explanation: Mandela was held on Robben Island for many of the years he was imprisoned for opposing apartheid.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What does the term democratic in the Preamble mean?
options: The country has a hereditary ruler
Rulers are elected by the people, who have equal political rights
questions.explanation: A democratic country is governed by representatives chosen by the people.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which statement describes the aim of justice in the Preamble?
options: Social, economic and political justice for all citizens
Justice only in courts of foreign countries
questions.explanation: The Preamble promises justice in social, economic and political life.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why is it important that India's Constituent Assembly included members from many communities and regions?
options: It reduced the number of laws
A constitution made with wide participation is more likely to be accepted by all
It removed the need for debate
questions.explanation: Broad representation gives the Constitution legitimacy across a diverse country.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why is the Constitution called the supreme law of the land?
options: All laws and government actions must follow it, or they can be declared invalid
It is longer than other laws
Only the President can read it
questions.explanation: Laws that go against the Constitution can be struck down by the courts.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What does fraternity mean in the Preamble?
questions.answer: Fraternity means a feeling of brotherhood and common belonging among all citizens. The Preamble links it to the dignity of the individual and the unity and integrity of the nation.
questions.explanation: Fraternity binds citizens of different backgrounds together.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Describe how South Africa made its democratic constitution after apartheid.
questions.answer: After the first multiracial elections in 1994, elected representatives of different groups worked together in an assembly to draft a new constitution. After negotiation and compromise, it was adopted in 1996 and guaranteed equal rights.
questions.explanation: Cooperation between former rivals created a shared constitution.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What is the minimum age to contest a Lok Sabha election?
questions.explanation: A candidate for the Lok Sabha must be at least twenty-five years old.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Who presides over the meetings of the Lok Sabha?
questions.explanation: The Speaker conducts the proceedings of the Lok Sabha.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which institution can declare a law unconstitutional if it violates the Constitution?
questions.explanation: This power is called judicial review.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: For how many years is a Rajya Sabha member elected?
questions.explanation: Rajya Sabha members serve six-year terms, with one-third retiring every two years.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why is the Prime Minister in practice the most powerful person in the Indian government?
options: The Prime Minister is the Chief Justice
The Prime Minister controls the courts
The Prime Minister is elected directly by all citizens
The Prime Minister leads the party or coalition with majority support in the Lok Sabha and heads the Cabinet
questions.explanation: The Cabinet takes major decisions, and the Prime Minister leads it with the backing of a majority.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Mention two functions of the Election Commission.
questions.answer: The Election Commission supervises the preparation of voters' lists, schedules elections and enforces the Model Code of Conduct. It also oversees counting of votes and declares results.
questions.explanation: It is an independent body that conducts elections.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why is the permanent executive important in running the government?
questions.answer: Civil servants remain in office when governments change, and they bring expertise and continuity. They carry out the decisions and policies of the political executive.
keyPoints: Remain in office as governments change
questions.explanation: Elected ministers decide policy, and officials put it into practice.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which Fundamental Right prohibits trafficking in human beings?
questions.explanation: The Right against Exploitation bans trafficking, forced labour and child labour in hazardous work.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Who protects and enforces the Fundamental Rights of citizens?
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court and High Courts can issue orders to enforce Fundamental Rights.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Under Article 21A, free and compulsory education is guaranteed to children in which age group?
questions.explanation: Article 21A was added in 2002 to make elementary education a Fundamental Right.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution abolishes untouchability?
questions.explanation: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: A person is arrested but not produced before a magistrate within 24 hours. Which right is mainly violated?
options: Right to Freedom, which protects personal liberty
questions.explanation: The Constitution gives protection to arrested persons, including being produced before a magistrate within twenty-four hours.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why can the government not take away Fundamental Rights through an ordinary law?
options: Fundamental Rights are guaranteed by the Constitution, and courts can strike down laws that violate them
Only the Army can change them
questions.explanation: The Constitution is above ordinary laws.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What is the Right against Exploitation? Mention two prohibitions under it.
questions.answer: The Right against Exploitation protects people from being forced to work or being treated as objects. It prohibits trafficking, forced labour and the employment of children below the age of fourteen in factories, mines or other hazardous work.
keyPoints: Bans child labour in hazardous work
questions.explanation: The right protects the weak against misuse by the powerful.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why are rights necessary in a democracy?
questions.answer: Rights protect individuals and minorities from the government and from the majority. They also give citizens the freedoms needed to take part in political life, such as speaking and forming associations.
questions.explanation: Without rights, voting alone would be meaningless.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Village Economy and People as Resource
questions.q: What does the term human capital refer to?
options: The skill, education and health of the people
questions.explanation: Human capital is the stock of skill and health that makes workers productive.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Village Economy and People as Resource
questions.q: Banking and transport belong to which sector?
questions.explanation: Services such as banking, transport and teaching are part of the tertiary sector.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Village Economy and People as Resource
questions.q: Which one of the following is a non-economic activity?
options: A farmer selling wheat in the market
A teacher working at a school
A mother cooking at home for her own family
questions.explanation: Work done for one's own family without payment is not counted as an economic activity.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Village Economy and People as Resource
questions.q: When farm work is available only in some months, the unemployment seen in the rest of the year is called
questions.explanation: Seasonal unemployment is common in agriculture.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Village Economy and People as Resource
questions.q: In a village where land is fixed, which step would most raise farm production?
options: Investing in irrigation, improved seeds and modern machines to raise yields
questions.explanation: Higher yields from the same land need more capital and better methods.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Village Economy and People as Resource
questions.q: Distinguish between economic and non-economic activities.
questions.answer: Economic activities produce goods and services that are counted in national income, such as farming, factory work and teaching. Non-economic activities, such as household work for one's own family, are done out of love or duty and are not paid.
keyPoints: Economic: produce goods and services for income
Non-economic: unpaid, for one's own family or duty
questions.explanation: Only economic activities contribute to national income.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Village Economy and People as Resource
questions.q: Suggest two ways in which the quality of a country's population can be improved.
questions.answer: The quality of population can be improved by investing in education, so that people learn skills, and in health care and nutrition, so that people are fit to work. Training and better living conditions also help.
questions.explanation: Healthy, skilled people are more productive.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What does availability of food mean in the idea of food security?
options: Food that is sold only abroad
Food production within the country, imports and stocks held by the government
questions.explanation: Availability means there is enough food in the country.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Green Revolution mainly increased the production of which crops?
questions.explanation: HYV seeds mostly raised the output of wheat and rice.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which of the following is a well-known milk cooperative in India?
questions.explanation: Amul, a cooperative of milk producers in Gujarat, is often cited as a successful model.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Who among the following is most likely to be food insecure?
questions.explanation: Those with no land and irregular income often cannot buy enough food.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why did India focus on self-sufficiency in food grains after independence?
options: To avoid dependence on imports and prevent famines such as the Bengal famine
questions.explanation: Self-sufficiency was seen as vital to protect the country from food shortage.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why did the Green Revolution mainly benefit states like Punjab and Haryana?
options: They had assured irrigation and farmers able to adopt new seeds and inputs
questions.explanation: New seeds needed dependable water and money for inputs, which these regions had.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What are the three dimensions of food security?
questions.answer: Food security has three dimensions: availability of food in the country, accessibility so that everyone can obtain it, and affordability so that people have the money to buy enough nutritious food.
questions.explanation: All three must hold for people to be food secure.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Explain how poverty and hunger are linked.
questions.answer: Poor families have low incomes and cannot buy enough nutritious food, so they go hungry. Hunger and poor health in turn reduce their strength and productivity, making it harder to earn and escape poverty.
questions.explanation: Poverty and hunger can reinforce each other.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which French thinker wrote the book The Social Contract?
questions.explanation: Rousseau argued that government gets its authority from an agreement among the people.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which thinker proposed the division of government power among the legislative, executive and judiciary in The Spirit of the Laws?
questions.explanation: Montesquieu proposed this separation of powers, which later influenced many constitutions.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Who wrote the Declaration of the Rights of Woman and Citizen in 1791?
questions.explanation: Olympe de Gouges criticised the Constitution for leaving out women and demanded equal rights.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: In which year did Napoleon crown himself Emperor of France?
questions.explanation: Napoleon made himself Emperor in 1804.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What was a main feature of Napoleon's Civil Code of 1804?
options: It ended privileges based on birth, made all equal before the law and protected private property
It restored the privileges of the nobility
It gave the Church control of courts
questions.explanation: The Code, also called the Napoleonic Code, spread ideas of legal equality across Europe.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What happened to slavery in the French colonies after the Convention freed the slaves in 1794?
options: It was extended to France itself
Napoleon reintroduced it, and it was finally abolished in 1848
questions.explanation: The ideas of liberty and equality were applied to the colonies only slowly.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: State the contribution of Montesquieu and Rousseau to political thought.
questions.answer: Montesquieu proposed the separation of governmental powers into legislative, executive and judicial branches. Rousseau argued in The Social Contract that government should rest on an agreement among free and equal people.
keyPoints: Rousseau: social contract based on the people's agreement
questions.explanation: Their ideas shaped revolutionary thinking in France.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: How did women take part in the French Revolution, and what did they demand?
questions.answer: Women worked, formed political clubs, wrote newspapers and joined marches. They demanded the right to vote, to hold political office and equal wages and education, though their clubs were banned in 1793.
keyPoints: Demanded the vote and equal rights
questions.explanation: Women's demands were not fully accepted at the time.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Before 1917 most Russians earned their living from
questions.explanation: Around eighty per cent of Russians were farmers.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Karl Marx argued that industrial society was divided mainly into which two classes?
questions.explanation: Marx said capitalists who owned factories exploited the workers who laboured in them.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why is the Bolshevik takeover of 1917 called the October Revolution although it happened in November by the western calendar?
options: It was planned for October but delayed
Russia then used a calendar about thirteen days behind the western one
The month was changed by Lenin
questions.explanation: Russia used the Julian calendar until 1918.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What was the outcome of the Russian Civil War of 1918-1920?
options: Russia broke into hundreds of states
questions.explanation: The Red Army, led by Trotsky, defeated the Whites and secured Bolshevik rule.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: How did the Soviet system of Five Year Plans differ from a free market economy?
options: The state set production targets instead of private firms responding to market prices
Private firms alone decided what to produce
Prices were decided by foreign countries
questions.explanation: In a planned economy the government decides what is produced and in what quantity.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Describe the condition of industrial workers in Russia before 1917.
questions.answer: Workers laboured for long hours for low wages in crowded factories and lived in poor housing. They had few rights and could not form strong unions, which led to strikes and protests.
questions.explanation: Harsh conditions made workers receptive to socialist ideas.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: How did liberals and socialists differ in their views on property?
questions.answer: Liberals supported individual rights and private property and wanted limited government. Socialists believed that property such as land and factories should be owned collectively, since private ownership led to inequality.
keyPoints: Liberals: private property and individual rights
Socialists linked private property to inequality
questions.explanation: The disagreement was central to nineteenth-century politics.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Nazism and the Rise of Hitler
questions.q: In which country was Adolf Hitler born?
questions.explanation: Hitler was born in Austria and later became a German leader.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Nazism and the Rise of Hitler
questions.q: Which of the following was a Nazi concentration and extermination camp?
questions.explanation: Auschwitz, in occupied Poland, was the largest of the Nazi camps.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Nazism and the Rise of Hitler
questions.q: Which fire in February 1933 was used by Hitler to suspend civil rights?
questions.explanation: After the fire in the Reichstag building, a decree suspended freedoms such as speech and assembly.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Nazism and the Rise of Hitler
questions.q: Which President of Germany appointed Hitler as Chancellor in 1933?
questions.explanation: President Hindenburg appointed Hitler on 30 January 1933.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Nazism and the Rise of Hitler
questions.q: Why did the Nazis take control of schools and teachers?
options: To teach loyalty to Hitler and Nazi racial ideas to children
To make schooling free for all
questions.explanation: Textbooks were rewritten and teachers were required to support the regime.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Nazism and the Rise of Hitler
questions.q: What was Kristallnacht?
questions.answer: Kristallnacht, or the Night of Broken Glass, was on 9-10 November 1938, when Nazi mobs and officials attacked Jewish homes, shops and synagogues across Germany. Many people were arrested.
keyPoints: Attacks on Jewish shops, homes and synagogues
questions.explanation: It marked a sharp increase in violence against Jews.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Nazism and the Rise of Hitler
questions.q: What were the consequences of the German invasion of Poland in 1939?
questions.answer: Britain and France declared war on Germany, which marked the start of the Second World War in Europe. The war later spread across many continents.
keyPoints: Start of the Second World War in Europe
questions.explanation: The invasion ended attempts to avoid a new European war.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which is the largest Indian state by area?
questions.explanation: Among the states, Rajasthan has the largest area.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Palk Strait separates India from which country?
questions.explanation: The Palk Strait lies between Tamil Nadu and Sri Lanka.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Through how many Indian states does the Tropic of Cancer pass?
questions.explanation: It passes through Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Peninsular India is surrounded by water on how many sides?
questions.explanation: The peninsula has the Arabian Sea on the west, the Indian Ocean on the south and the Bay of Bengal on the east.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why does India follow a single Indian Standard Time throughout the country?
options: Because the sun rises at the same time everywhere
To avoid confusion in railways, broadcasting and administration across the country
Because the country has no eastern part
questions.explanation: One common time, based on the Standard Meridian, helps coordination across the country.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Name any four countries that share a land border with India.
questions.answer: India shares land borders with Pakistan, Afghanistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Myanmar and Bangladesh.
questions.explanation: Sri Lanka and the Maldives are island neighbours.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Distinguish between the Peninsular Plateau and the Northern Plains in terms of rocks and soil.
questions.answer: The Peninsular Plateau is made of old, hard crystalline rocks, has an uneven surface and is rich in minerals. The Northern Plains are made of alluvium deposited by rivers, are flat and have fertile soil.
keyPoints: Plateau: old hard rocks, uneven, mineral-rich
questions.explanation: The two regions differ in origin and in use.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Through which state does the Brahmaputra enter India?
questions.explanation: The river enters India in Arunachal Pradesh, where it is called the Dihang.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: A river together with its tributaries is called a
questions.explanation: The Ganga river system, for example, includes the Ganga and its tributaries.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Hirakud Dam is built on which river?
questions.explanation: The Hirakud Dam in Odisha is on the Mahanadi.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which two rivers together form the Sundarbans delta?
questions.explanation: The Ganga and Brahmaputra build the world's largest delta, including the Sundarbans.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why did early civilisations often develop along river valleys?
options: Rivers gave fertile soil, water for farming and drinking, and routes for trade
There were no rivers in deserts
questions.explanation: Fertile land and water supported farming and settlements.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What happens to a river as its gradient decreases on the plains?
options: It flows faster and cuts deep gorges
It slows down, deposits silt and forms meanders and floodplains
questions.explanation: A slow river cannot carry its load and drops silt, creating bends and floodplains.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Distinguish between a tributary and a distributary.
questions.answer: A tributary is a smaller stream that joins a main river. A distributary is a branch that splits off from the main river, usually near its mouth in a delta, and flows away from it.
keyPoints: Distributary branches away from the main river
questions.explanation: Deltas have many distributaries.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: How can excess use of river water upstream cause problems for areas downstream?
questions.answer: If too much water is taken out for irrigation or industry upstream, less water reaches downstream areas, which may face shortages for farming and drinking. It can also reduce the silt reaching deltas and cause disputes between regions.
questions.explanation: Rivers are shared resources.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Kalbaisakhi is a pre-monsoon storm that occurs mainly in
questions.explanation: Kalbaisakhi brings thunderstorms to West Bengal and nearby areas in the hot season.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The retreating monsoon season occurs mainly in
questions.explanation: From October the monsoon winds withdraw from the country.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What is a feature of the south-west monsoon season?
options: Extremely cold nights over the plains
Dry winds from the north-west only
Most of India's annual rainfall falls in this season
questions.explanation: The south-west monsoon brings the bulk of the annual rain between June and September.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: When does the monsoon usually first reach the Kerala coast?
questions.explanation: The monsoon reaches Kerala in the first week of June and then spreads across the country.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why do Indian farmers plan their sowing around the arrival of the monsoon?
options: Most crops depend on monsoon water since irrigation is limited in many areas
questions.explanation: Timely rain decides the success of many kharif crops.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What is a rain shadow area?
questions.answer: A rain shadow area is the leeward side of a mountain that receives little rain because the moist winds have already shed their moisture on the windward side. The Deccan Plateau behind the Western Ghats is an example.
questions.explanation: Mountains can create very different rainfall on two sides.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why do the hills of north-eastern India receive very heavy rainfall?
questions.answer: The hills stand in the path of moist winds from the Bay of Bengal, which are forced to rise and cool, causing heavy rain. Funnel-shaped hills in places such as Meghalaya further trap the winds.
keyPoints: Moist winds from the Bay of Bengal
questions.explanation: Relief and wind direction explain the high rainfall.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which big cat is the national animal of India?
questions.explanation: The tiger is India's national animal.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Acacia and babool are typical of which type of vegetation?
questions.explanation: Thorny plants grow in dry areas with little rain.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: How does a wildlife sanctuary usually differ from a national park?
options: A sanctuary may allow some regulated human activity, while a national park has stronger protection
A sanctuary is only for plants
They are identical in every way
questions.explanation: National parks have stricter rules on human use of the area.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which animal lives at high altitude in the Himalayas?
questions.explanation: The snow leopard lives in the high Himalayan region.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: In which year was the Wildlife Protection Act passed in India?
questions.explanation: The Wildlife Protection Act of 1972 banned hunting of many species and set up protected areas.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why are endangered animals more at risk when forests are cut into small patches?
options: Small isolated groups have less food and fewer mates, so they can be wiped out easily
questions.explanation: Habitat fragmentation isolates populations and reduces their chances of survival.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What do the terms flora and fauna mean?
questions.answer: Flora means the plants of a region or period, and fauna means the animals of that region or period.
questions.explanation: Together they describe the wildlife of a region.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Explain how overgrazing and deforestation harm natural vegetation.
questions.answer: Overgrazing by animals strips the grass cover and prevents new growth, while deforestation removes trees and exposes the soil to erosion. Both reduce vegetation and damage habitats.
questions.explanation: Both practices degrade land and reduce biodiversity.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which of the following is a primary activity?
questions.explanation: Primary activities use natural resources directly, such as farming, mining and fishing.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Population density is generally high in
options: Fertile river plains and coastal areas
questions.explanation: Fertile land and water attract settlement.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What is meant by the natural increase of population?
questions.explanation: Natural increase is the difference between births and deaths, not counting migration.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What does urbanisation mean?
options: Growth in the number of villages
A rise in the share of people living in towns and cities
questions.explanation: Urbanisation occurs as people move to cities and as towns grow.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why is a high proportion of dependants a burden on an economy?
options: Fewer workers must support more children and elderly persons
It reduces the need for schools
questions.explanation: Each worker has to support more people, leaving less to save and invest.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why do many Indian cities face problems such as congestion and slums?
options: A large inflow of migrants is greater than the housing and services available
Cities have no jobs for anyone
questions.explanation: Rapid migration puts pressure on housing, transport and services.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Name the three main age groups used to describe the age composition of a population.
questions.answer: The three age groups are children (0 to 14 years), the working-age group (15 to 59 years) and the aged (60 years and above).
questions.explanation: Age structure shows how many dependants each worker supports.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why are adolescents considered an important resource for the nation, and what do they need?
questions.answer: Adolescents are the future workforce and citizens, so their energy and skills will shape the country. They need good nutrition, education, health care and training to develop their abilities.
questions.explanation: Investment in adolescents pays off in later years.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What is a key difference between a democracy and a monarchy?
options: In a democracy rulers are chosen by the people, and are not born into power
questions.explanation: Democratic rulers get their position through elections, not heredity.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What does rule of law mean?
options: Everyone, including rulers, must obey the law
questions.explanation: Rule of law means no person is above the law.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why do democracies hold regular elections?
options: To let citizens choose or change rulers peacefully and hold them accountable
questions.explanation: Regular elections allow citizens to reward or remove rulers.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which of these goes against democratic principles?
options: Jailing journalists who criticise the government
questions.explanation: Freedom of expression is essential to democracy.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why is it wrong to claim that democracy automatically guarantees faster economic growth?
options: Growth depends on many factors, and democracy alone does not guarantee it, though it protects rights
questions.explanation: Economic outcomes depend on many conditions, and democracy is valued for other reasons as well.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What does accountability mean in a democracy?
questions.answer: Accountability means that rulers must explain and answer for their decisions to the people and their representatives, and can be removed through elections if people are not satisfied.
keyPoints: Rulers must answer for their actions
People can remove them through elections
questions.explanation: Accountability keeps power in check.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why should citizens have the right to disagree with the government in a democracy?
questions.answer: Disagreement helps to point out mistakes and improve policy, and it protects minorities from being ignored. A democracy that silences criticism cannot correct its errors.
questions.explanation: Open dissent is necessary to correct wrong decisions.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: On which date is Republic Day celebrated in India?
questions.explanation: It marks the day in 1950 when the Constitution came into force.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: In which year did South Africa adopt its democratic constitution?
questions.explanation: South Africa's constitution was adopted in 1996, after the first multiracial elections.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What resolution did the Indian National Congress pass at its Lahore session in 1929?
questions.explanation: The Lahore session declared complete independence as the goal of the national movement.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Preamble begins with the words We, the people of India. What does this signify?
options: Power ultimately rests with the people
Only some people made the Constitution
The Constitution was written by foreign rulers
questions.explanation: It shows that the Constitution gets its authority from the people.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why was the Objectives Resolution of 1946 important?
options: It laid down the goals and principles that guided the drafting of the Constitution
questions.explanation: Its ideals were later reflected in the Preamble.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: State two things that a constitution does in a country.
questions.answer: A constitution sets out the basic rules on how the government is formed and what powers it has. It also guarantees citizens' rights and limits the government's power.
keyPoints: Sets rules for forming and running government
questions.explanation: A constitution is the basic law of the country.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why did leaders of India's national movement want a constitution that guaranteed rights?
questions.answer: Under colonial rule, people's freedoms such as speech and association were restricted. Leaders wanted an independent India to protect these freedoms and to ensure equality and democratic government.
questions.explanation: Experience of colonial restrictions shaped their vision.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What does EVM stand for?
questions.explanation: Electronic Voting Machines are used to record votes in Indian elections.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What is a person who contests an election called?
questions.explanation: A candidate is a person who stands for election.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The party that wins a majority forms the government. What is the group of members who do not support the government called?
questions.explanation: The opposition criticises the government and offers alternatives.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Who elects the President of India?
options: Elected members of Parliament and of State Legislative Assemblies
questions.explanation: The President is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: How many representatives does each Lok Sabha constituency elect?
questions.explanation: Each constituency elects one member to the Lok Sabha.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why is the Election Commission made independent of the government?
options: So it can obey the ruling party
So it can avoid holding elections
So it can change election results
So it can conduct elections fairly without pressure from the ruling party
questions.explanation: Independence helps maintain free and fair elections.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What is judicial review?
questions.answer: Judicial review is the power of the courts, especially the Supreme Court, to examine laws and actions of the government and to declare them invalid if they go against the Constitution.
keyPoints: Can declare them invalid if unconstitutional
questions.explanation: It protects the supremacy of the Constitution.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What does it mean that the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha?
questions.answer: It means that all ministers together are answerable to the Lok Sabha for the working of the government. If the Lok Sabha loses confidence in the government, the whole Council of Ministers must resign.
keyPoints: Government needs the confidence of the Lok Sabha
Must resign if confidence is lost
questions.explanation: This keeps the executive under the control of the elected House.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Under which Fundamental Right can citizens form a trade union?
questions.explanation: The Right to Freedom includes the freedom to form associations and unions.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which Fundamental Right says that all persons are equal before the law?
questions.explanation: The Right to Equality guarantees equality before law and equal protection of laws.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What is a Public Interest Litigation?
options: A case that only the victim may file
A case filed by the police only
A case that cannot be heard in court
A case through which any person may approach the court in the interest of the public
questions.explanation: PIL allows people to seek justice for issues that affect the public.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which writ is an order asking an official to perform a duty he or she has failed to do?
questions.explanation: Mandamus means we command, and it orders a public authority to carry out its duty.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: A person is held in custody illegally. Which writ can help to secure their release?
questions.explanation: Habeas corpus requires that a detained person be produced before the court.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: State two features of the Right to Freedom of Religion.
questions.answer: Every person is free to profess, practise and propagate any religion, and groups may manage their own religious affairs. The state has no official religion and treats all religions equally.
keyPoints: Freedom to profess, practise and propagate
questions.explanation: India is a secular state.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why do minorities need cultural and educational rights?
questions.answer: These rights protect minorities' language, script and culture from being overshadowed by the majority. They allow minorities to set up their own educational institutions to pass on their heritage.
questions.explanation: Equal respect for different cultures is part of democracy.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Village Economy and People as Resource
questions.q: Cotton textile manufacturing belongs to which sector?
questions.explanation: The secondary sector turns raw materials into finished goods.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Village Economy and People as Resource
questions.q: What is a tubewell mainly used for in farming?
questions.explanation: A tubewell draws groundwater to irrigate fields.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Village Economy and People as Resource
questions.q: Why is irrigation important for multiple cropping?
options: It increases the area of land
Crops need water through the year, not only in the rainy season
questions.explanation: Reliable water allows more than one crop to be grown on the same land in a year.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Village Economy and People as Resource
questions.q: What does it mean when population is called an asset?
options: Educated and healthy people contribute to production and growth
questions.explanation: A trained and healthy population becomes human capital.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Village Economy and People as Resource
questions.q: Which example shows a shift of activity from the primary to the secondary sector?
options: Turning sugarcane into sugar or jaggery in a mill
questions.explanation: Processing a raw product into another good is secondary activity.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Village Economy and People as Resource
questions.q: Why is unemployment among educated youth a concern for a country?
options: It wastes the human capital the country invested in
questions.explanation: Educated people who cannot find work do not contribute to growth as they could.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Village Economy and People as Resource
questions.q: Explain the terms fixed capital and working capital with one example each.
questions.answer: Fixed capital means tools, machines and buildings that last for many years, such as a tractor. Working capital means raw materials and money in hand that are used up in production, such as seeds.
keyPoints: Fixed capital: lasting tools and machines
Working capital: raw materials and money used up
questions.explanation: Both are kinds of physical capital.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Village Economy and People as Resource
questions.q: Describe how electricity and tubewells helped farmers to irrigate more land.
questions.answer: Electricity-run tubewells could pump groundwater faster and irrigate larger areas than older methods. This allowed farmers to grow more than one crop a year and raised production.
questions.explanation: Better irrigation expanded cultivation.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which of these items is commonly sold at ration shops?
questions.explanation: Ration shops sell essential food grains and sugar at fixed prices.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What does the mid-day meal scheme provide?
questions.explanation: It gives school children a cooked meal, improving nutrition and attendance.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which group is among the most vulnerable to poverty in India?
options: Landless agricultural labourers and casual workers
questions.explanation: Those without land or regular work earn low and uncertain incomes.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What is a subsidy?
options: A tax paid to the government
A bank loan with high interest
Money paid by the government to lower the price consumers pay
questions.explanation: Food subsidies reduce the price of grain for consumers.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why does a drought raise the risk of hunger?
options: Crop failure lowers food supply and farm incomes, while prices rise
questions.explanation: Less food and less income make it harder for families to buy enough to eat.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What is the minimum support price?
questions.answer: The minimum support price is a price announced by the government at which it will buy certain crops from farmers, such as wheat and rice. It protects farmers from very low market prices.
keyPoints: Government buys crops at this price
questions.explanation: It supports farmers and helps build buffer stocks.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: How does the Public Distribution System help poor families when market prices rise?
questions.answer: Ration shops sell grain and other items at fixed, lower prices, so poor families are less affected by market price rises. The buffer stock held by the government helps to keep these supplies available.
keyPoints: Fixed lower prices at ration shops
questions.explanation: The system protects consumers against rising food prices.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which colours make up the French tricolour flag?
questions.explanation: The tricolour of blue, white and red became the symbol of the French nation.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which words formed the motto of the French Revolution?
questions.explanation: These three ideals were central to the Revolution.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which queen of France, the wife of Louis XVI, was executed in 1793?
questions.explanation: Marie Antoinette was tried and guillotined in October 1793.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Where was the royal court of Louis XVI based?
questions.explanation: Versailles was the splendid palace of the French kings, outside Paris.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: How did economic problems help to bring about the French Revolution?
options: Taxes were abolished for the Third Estate
Wars and royal spending emptied the treasury, bad harvests raised bread prices and heavy taxes burdened the Third Estate
questions.explanation: Financial crisis and hunger combined to cause widespread anger.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What was the Tennis Court Oath?
questions.answer: In June 1789 members of the Third Estate, who had declared themselves the National Assembly, gathered in an indoor tennis court at Versailles. They swore not to separate until they had drafted a constitution for France.
keyPoints: Gathered at an indoor tennis court in Versailles
questions.explanation: It showed the determination of the National Assembly.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Explain how the ideas of the French Revolution spread beyond France.
questions.answer: Napoleon's armies and his Civil Code carried ideas such as equality before the law and the end of feudal privileges to other parts of Europe. The ideals of liberty and equality also inspired movements for rights and freedom elsewhere, including in colonies.
keyPoints: Ideas of liberty and equality spread
questions.explanation: The Revolution's ideals had a lasting influence on the world.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What is rule by one person with unlimited power called?
questions.explanation: The Tsar ruled as an autocrat.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: In the First World War, Russia fought on the same side as Britain and France against which country?
questions.explanation: Russia fought against Germany and Austria-Hungary.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Who emerged as the leader of the Soviet Union after Lenin's death in 1924?
questions.explanation: Stalin gradually gained control of the Communist Party and the state.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What happened to the land of nobles and the Church after the Bolsheviks took power?
options: It was returned to the Tsar
It was sold to foreign companies
It was taken over and given to peasants
questions.explanation: Land reform was among the first measures of the Bolshevik government.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why did socialists such as Robert Owen set up cooperative communities?
options: To show people could live and work cooperatively and share property instead of competing for profit
questions.explanation: Owen's community at New Harmony in America was an attempt to put cooperative ideas into practice.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Name two political groups that opposed the Tsar's rule in Russia.
questions.answer: Opposition groups included the Bolsheviks and Mensheviks, who were socialists, the Socialist Revolutionaries, who represented peasants, and liberals who wanted a constitution.
questions.explanation: Several groups with different aims opposed the autocracy.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Marx expected revolutions in industrial countries, yet Russia, a mainly agricultural country, had one first. Give two reasons.
questions.answer: The Tsar's autocracy was weak and unpopular, and military defeats in the First World War worsened shortages and anger. Peasants wanted land, and workers in the big factories of cities were organised and ready to strike.
keyPoints: Defeats and shortages in the war
questions.explanation: Discontent among both peasants and workers combined with war to topple the Tsar.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Nazism and the Rise of Hitler
questions.q: What title did Hitler take as the supreme leader of Nazi Germany?
questions.explanation: Fuhrer means leader.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Nazism and the Rise of Hitler
questions.q: By what name is Hitler's regime in Germany from 1933 to 1945 also known?
questions.explanation: The Nazis called their state the Third Reich.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Nazism and the Rise of Hitler
questions.q: What was the Munich Putsch of 1923?
options: A failed attempt by Hitler to seize power in Bavaria
A victory parade of the army
An election won by the Nazis
questions.explanation: Hitler was arrested after the attempt and wrote Mein Kampf in prison.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Nazism and the Rise of Hitler
questions.q: What role did the Nazis expect women to play in society?
options: Mothers and homemakers who raised children, with fewer career opportunities
questions.explanation: Nazi ideology limited women's role mainly to the home and family.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Nazism and the Rise of Hitler
questions.q: How did German rearmament in the 1930s affect the economy?
options: It created jobs through arms and public works, but also made war more likely
questions.explanation: Spending on arms and public works reduced unemployment while preparing for war.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Nazism and the Rise of Hitler
questions.q: Why is Nazi Germany described as a totalitarian state?
options: It allowed full freedom of the press
It tried to control every part of life, including politics, media, education and culture
It left people free to decide their beliefs
questions.explanation: A totalitarian state seeks total control over society.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Nazism and the Rise of Hitler
questions.q: What does the word propaganda mean?
questions.answer: Propaganda is the spreading of information, ideas or slogans, often one-sided or misleading, to influence what people think and to win support for a cause.
questions.explanation: Nazi Germany used propaganda on a large scale.

questions.subject: social
questions.topic: Nazism and the Rise of Hitler
questions.q: Describe how the Nazis dealt with political opponents after 1933.
questions.answer: The Nazis banned other political parties and trade unions, censored the press, and used the Gestapo to arrest opponents. Many were sent to concentration camps, which created fear and silenced opposition.
keyPoints: Arrests by the Gestapo and camps
questions.explanation: The regime used terror and control to remove opposition.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which ocean lies to the south of India?
questions.explanation: India lies on the northern edge of the Indian Ocean.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: In which direction from India do the Himalayas lie?
questions.explanation: The Himalayas form a long arc along India's northern border.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which landform lies between the Western Ghats and the Arabian Sea?
questions.explanation: The western coastal plain is a narrow strip between the Ghats and the sea.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The black soil of the Deccan Plateau was formed from
questions.explanation: Lava flows weathered to make the black soil, which suits cotton.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why are the rivers of the northern plains useful for transport?
options: They flow across gently sloping plains, which lets boats travel
questions.explanation: Slow-moving rivers on flat land can be used for navigation.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why are large deltas found along the east coast of India?
options: Large east-flowing rivers deposit silt at their mouths in the Bay of Bengal
The east coast has no rivers
The coast is covered with ice
questions.explanation: The Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri build deltas on the east coast.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Name any four physiographic divisions of India.
questions.answer: The main divisions are the Himalayan Mountains, the Northern Plains, the Peninsular Plateau, the Indian Desert, the Coastal Plains and the Islands.
questions.explanation: Each division has its own relief and features.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: How do the Himalayas differ from the Peninsular Plateau in age and formation?
questions.answer: The Himalayas are young fold mountains formed by the folding of rocks when plates collided, and they are still rising. The Peninsular Plateau is an ancient block of hard crystalline rock, much older and more stable.
keyPoints: Himalayas: young fold mountains, still rising
questions.explanation: The two regions have very different geological histories.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: From which glacier does the Bhagirathi, the source stream of the Ganga, begin?
questions.explanation: The Bhagirathi rises from the Gangotri glacier in the Himalayas.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Into which water body does the Kaveri flow?
questions.explanation: The Kaveri flows east across southern India to the Bay of Bengal.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi and Beas are tributaries of which river system?
questions.explanation: They are the rivers of the Punjab region that join the Indus system.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What are the main benefits of the Bhakra Nangal project on the Sutlej?
questions.explanation: The dam stores water for irrigation and generates electricity.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: How can dams help in controlling floods?
options: They store excess water during heavy rain and release it gradually
They remove all water from rivers
questions.explanation: Stored water reduces the sudden rise in river level during heavy rain.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Name three east-flowing rivers of peninsular India.
questions.answer: The Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri are east-flowing rivers that drain into the Bay of Bengal.
questions.explanation: They flow eastward across the Deccan Plateau.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why are peninsular rivers less suitable for navigation than the Ganga?
questions.answer: Peninsular rivers are seasonal and carry little water in dry months, and they flow over uneven plateau land with waterfalls and rapids. This makes boat travel difficult compared with the slow, perennial Ganga on the plains.
keyPoints: Waterfalls and rapids on the plateau
Ganga flows on gentle plains all year
questions.explanation: Navigation needs steady water and gentle slopes.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The south-west monsoon season in India lasts from
questions.explanation: The monsoon rains cover most of India between June and September.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The word monsoon comes from the Arabic word mausim, which means
questions.explanation: Arab traders used the word for the seasonal winds of the Indian Ocean.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: How do ocean currents affect the climate of a coastal area?
options: Warm currents raise coastal temperatures and cold currents lower them
They change the length of the day
questions.explanation: The temperature of the water influences the air over nearby land.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which of these places has an extreme or continental climate?
questions.explanation: Delhi is far from the sea and has hot summers and cold winters.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why is the range of temperature small in southern India?
options: It is near the equator and has a moderating influence from the surrounding sea
It is surrounded by high mountains
questions.explanation: Nearness to the equator and the sea keeps temperatures fairly even through the year.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why do farmers in Punjab grow wheat in winter rather than in summer?
options: Wheat needs cool weather and gains from winter rain from western disturbances
questions.explanation: Wheat is a rabi crop grown in the cool season.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Describe two features of the cold weather season in India.
questions.answer: Temperatures are lowest in the north, with clear skies and cool, dry winds blowing from land to sea. Some winter rain falls in the north-west from western disturbances.
keyPoints: Low temperatures, especially in the north
questions.explanation: The season runs from about December to February.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why does rainfall in the Ganga plain generally decrease from east to west?
questions.answer: The monsoon winds bring moisture from the Bay of Bengal, which is shed as rain as they move inland. By the time they reach the west, such as Delhi, they carry less moisture, so rainfall in Kolkata is greater than in Delhi.
keyPoints: Moisture from the Bay of Bengal
Winds lose moisture as they move inland
questions.explanation: Distance from the source of moisture reduces rainfall.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The Sundarbans are famous for which type of forest?
questions.explanation: The Sundarbans in the Ganga delta have extensive mangroves.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: In which region are elephants mainly found in India?
options: The forests of Kerala, Karnataka and Assam
questions.explanation: Elephants live in wooded areas in the south and north-east.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which of the following is a well-known bird sanctuary in Rajasthan?
questions.explanation: Keoladeo National Park at Bharatpur is famous for its water birds.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What does the term biodiversity mean?
options: The variety of living organisms in an area
questions.explanation: Biodiversity includes the variety of plants, animals and microorganisms.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why is protecting habitats important for saving species?
options: Animals depend on their habitat for food and shelter, so protecting it saves many species together
questions.explanation: Conserving ecosystems helps all the species that live in them.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What is an endangered species? Name one from India.
questions.answer: An endangered species is one whose numbers have fallen so low that it is at risk of becoming extinct. The Bengal tiger is an example from India.
keyPoints: Numbers very low, at risk of extinction
An example such as the Bengal tiger
questions.explanation: Such species need special protection.

crossCheck.note: The Bengal tiger is correctly listed as endangered, but the one-horned rhinoceros is classed as Vulnerable by IUCN rather than Endangered. Accept only if the textbook uses a looser sense of the word. Fixed after review: the one-horned rhinoceros is IUCN Vulnerable, so it was removed.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: How can local communities help to conserve forests?
questions.answer: Communities can plant trees, protect forests from illegal cutting and fires, and use forest produce carefully. Working with forest officials, they can guard wildlife and share in the benefits of conservation.
questions.explanation: Local participation makes conservation more effective.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: The number of children born per 1000 persons in a year is called the
questions.explanation: The birth rate measures births per thousand people in a year.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What is the Census?
options: A count of the population along with the collection of other data about it
questions.explanation: The Census collects information about the number, age, occupation and literacy of people.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why do coastal plains often have a high population?
options: They have ports, fertile land and a moderate climate
questions.explanation: Trade, farming and a mild climate attract settlement.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: How can better health care affect population growth over time?
options: It always raises the death rate
Death rates fall and growth rises at first, but better health and education can later lower birth rates
questions.explanation: Falling death rates raise growth first, and fewer births follow as families become healthier and better informed.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why is women's education linked with lower birth rates?
options: Educated women are forbidden to marry
Educated women tend to marry later, plan families and have more health knowledge
questions.explanation: Studies show that education gives women greater choice and awareness.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What is meant by the occupational structure of a population?
questions.answer: The occupational structure is the distribution of the working population among different kinds of work, usually grouped into primary, secondary and tertiary activities.
keyPoints: Distribution of workers by type of work
questions.explanation: It shows how a country earns its living.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Suggest two measures to control the rapid growth of population.
questions.answer: Spreading education, especially among girls and women, and creating awareness about family planning can slow growth. Better health care that lowers infant deaths also encourages smaller families.
questions.explanation: Social change helps reduce birth rates.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: In a democracy, each adult citizen has
questions.explanation: Political equality means one person, one vote.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which of these is an example of political equality?
options: Every adult citizen has the right to vote
questions.explanation: In a democracy all adults have an equal right to vote.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What is a referendum?
options: A direct vote by citizens on a specific question or issue
questions.explanation: In a referendum citizens vote directly on a proposal.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: In a democracy the majority must also
questions.explanation: Majority rule works only when minorities are protected.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which situation best shows a country moving away from democracy?
options: The ruling party postpones elections indefinitely and bans criticism
The press freely reports on the government
questions.explanation: Postponing elections and silencing critics weaken accountability.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why does a democracy leave room for correcting mistakes?
options: Citizens can criticise and vote out rulers, so errors become visible and can be changed
questions.explanation: Open debate and elections let the public respond to bad decisions.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What do we mean by free and fair elections?
questions.answer: In free and fair elections every adult can vote, parties and candidates are free to compete, voting is secret and results are not rigged or influenced by fear or force.
keyPoints: Secret ballot and no pressure or rigging
questions.explanation: Fair rules give voters a real choice.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why is democracy sometimes called government by discussion?
questions.answer: In a democracy decisions are made after debate and consultation among representatives and citizens, and different views are heard before laws are passed. Discussion helps reach decisions that more people can accept.
questions.explanation: Discussion is at the heart of democratic decision making.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Who was the first Prime Minister of independent India?
questions.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru became the first Prime Minister in 1947.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Who is popularly known as the Father of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: Dr Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee and played a leading role in framing the Constitution.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What does liberty in the Preamble stand for?
options: Freedom of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship
questions.explanation: Liberty means that citizens are free to think, express and believe as they choose within the law.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What does equality in the Preamble ensure?
options: Equality of status and of opportunity
questions.explanation: Equality means all citizens are equal before law and have equal opportunities.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which event shows that the Constitution limits the power of the government?
options: A court strikes down a law that violates a Fundamental Right
A new law is passed by Parliament
questions.explanation: Courts can cancel laws that break the Constitution.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What is the difference between the date on which the Indian Constitution was adopted and the date on which it came into force?
questions.answer: The Constitution was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26 November 1949 and came into force on 26 January 1950, which is celebrated as Republic Day.
questions.explanation: The January date was chosen to recall the 1930 declaration of independence.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why did the framers of the Constitution choose universal adult franchise from the beginning?
questions.answer: Leaders of the national movement believed in equality, so every adult citizen should have a say in government regardless of wealth, caste or sex. Giving the vote to all gave the new democracy a broad base.
questions.explanation: Universal franchise made political equality real.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Where do voters cast their votes on polling day?
questions.explanation: Voters go to polling booths in their area to cast their votes.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What is the purpose of voting by secret ballot?
options: To let voters choose freely without fear or pressure
To help candidates know who voted for them
questions.explanation: Secrecy protects voters from pressure.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Who is the head of the government in a State?
questions.explanation: The Chief Minister heads the State government, while the Governor is the formal head of the State.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which body can remove the Council of Ministers through a vote of no confidence?
questions.explanation: The Council of Ministers must have the confidence of the Lok Sabha to stay in office.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Why does the Lok Sabha have more power than the Rajya Sabha on money matters?
options: It is chosen by the President
It is directly elected by the people and the government needs its confidence
questions.explanation: Since the government is responsible to the Lok Sabha, it controls the budget.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What is a party manifesto?
questions.answer: A manifesto is a document issued by a political party before elections that states its policies and promises to voters about what it will do if it comes to power.
keyPoints: Issued by a party before elections
questions.explanation: Voters use manifestos to compare parties.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Explain why the President is called the nominal head while the Prime Minister is the real executive.
questions.answer: The President is the formal head of the state, but acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister. The Prime Minister and the Cabinet take the real decisions and run the government.
keyPoints: Acts on the advice of the ministers
Prime Minister and Cabinet take real decisions
questions.explanation: Real power rests with the elected government.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which Fundamental Right lets a person take up any profession or occupation?
questions.explanation: The Right to Freedom includes the freedom to practise any profession.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: What are human rights?
options: Rights that belong to every person simply because they are human
questions.explanation: Human rights are basic rights to which every person is entitled.

questions.subject: social
questions.q: Which situation violates the Right to Equality?
options: A school holds a sports day
A citizen votes in an election
A notice for a government post says that only men may apply, though women are equally qualified
questions.explanation: Discrimination on the ground of sex in public employment violates equality.
